transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Carlos Reyes (CTO - NimblePay), Maya Patel (ML Engineer), Jordan Lee (Infra)

Summary: Quick weekly POC check-in to review last week's bench results, confirm onboarding progress (VPC peering, SAML), discuss tuning for latency/cost, and align next steps for Dedicated pilot. Transcript has occasional automated transcription errors.

Topics: onboarding status, access setup (VPC peering / IAM / KMS), bench results (latency, tokens/sec, cost estimates), quantization and caching, safety / security questions, next steps and owners.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in for the NimblePay POC. we've got 60 minutes but we'll aim for 45. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Carlos: good, thanks. been heads down on other things but we have the infra folks on the call today to move the peering along.
[00:20] Jordan: yeah Jordan here, I have the peering ticket opened last night, i think i shared the CIDR in the ticket but i'll recap.
[00:28] Priya: awesome, great. quick agenda
  go through the bench numbers Priya ran last week, discuss the access blockers (vpc, iam, kms), tuning notes for quantization and batching, and agree next steps.
[00:42] Maya: sounds good.
[00:45] Alex: ok Priya, can you start with a 2 minute rundown of bench results?
[00:50] Priya: sure. so we ran two main runs: hosted baseline against rwu-v1 (Redwood eval alias) and a quantized 8-bit run on the Dedicated-equivalent nodes. hosted avg latency for our 512 token test prompt was ~210ms per token tail-latency 95th at 420ms, throughput 120 tokens/s. Dedicated quantized run dropped token latency to ~160ms and improved tokens/sec to 185. cost per 1k tokens estimated about 0.70 on hosted vs 0.42 on Dedicated assuming reserved commit. caveat: these numbers are noisy
  seq length distribution matters and we saw cold-start variance. also caching (prefix) brought down CPU on the host tests by about 20% when we used the long-prompt cache.
[01:45] Carlos: so that's in the spreadsheet you linked earlier? i couldn't access it last night.
[01:50] Priya: yes link is in the deck
  https://redwood.com/pocs/nimblepay-bench.xlsx
  but i think the permissions were off, sorry about that. alex will re-share with correct perms after the meeting.
[01:59] Alex: i'll resend. apologies for the permission hiccup.
[02:05] Jordan: quick infra q
  for Dedicated you're saying KMS needs to be reachable by the test service account? we prefer to use our own KMS and HSM.
[02:14] Priya: yes you can bring your own KMS. for the private/deploy we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS via workload identity. you'll need to grant the test service account encryption/decryption permissions.
[02:27] Jordan: ok we'll make a policy, i'll drop it in the ticket.
[02:30] Maya: there's a question about data retention
  for logs and traces, can we set retention to 30 days and ensure no raw prompt storage?
[02:37] Alex: yes, Redwood's hosted defaults store logs for 90 days but for Dedicated we can configure retention and exclude raw prompts. we'll include the security package link.
[02:45] Carlos: that's important; our compliance team needs that documented.
[02:48] Alex: totally. we'll add the SOC2/ISO docs to the shared folder.
[02:52] Priya: wanted to call out one oddity from the bench
  when we ran the long-context (2k tokens) workload the KV cash
  uh KV cache
  warmed slower on the Dedicated emu; we suspect kernel selection for long seqs needs tuning. redwood runtime team saw similar on some P3-equivalent infra and have a tuning flag that we can enable to prefer attention kernels for long sequences, will test that in the next run.
[03:20] Carlos: interesting, we do have a lot of long invoices. what's the impact to latency when that flag is on vs off?
[03:28] Priya: it helped tail latency 95th by ~15% on long sequences in our internal tests but increased peak GPU memory marginally. for NimblePay, we could run the flag in canary and measure.
[03:39] Maya: would that affect cost materially?
[03:42] Priya: small change; more memory sometimes needs bigger instance size or more packing, but overall tokens/sec improved so cost per token stayed flat or slightly improved.
[03:50] Alex: ok good. next, onboarding status
  Carlos, Jordan, where are we with the VPC peering and SAML?
[03:58] Carlos: we've created the peering request, Jordan added the CIDR; we still need Redwood's peering request details and the SAML metadata.
[04:06] Jordan: yes and firewall rules
  i need the destination ports and service account IPs.
[04:12] Alex: i'll drop a peering template and the exact IP ranges. Priya will include the service account name for KMS access.
[04:18] Priya: i'll post exact ports (gRPC 443, metrics 9000 for the console, plus port for health checks) in the ticket.
[04:24] Jordan: perfect. one more thing: do you support identity federation via SAML2 with SCIM provisioning?
[04:30] Alex: yes, SAML via Azure/Okta supported + SCIM for provisioning users. we'll send a SAML metadata file.
[04:36] Carlos: timeline question
  we want a pilot by EOW next week is that realistic?
[04:42] Priya: depends on peering and KMS; if peering and KMS access are done by Tue/Wed we can schedule the Dedicated spin up and run benches by end of next week. so yes conditional.
[04:53] Maya: what about fallback
  if Dedicated isn't ready can we use hosted with VPC egress?
[04:58] Alex: yes we can run hosted for initial function tests; latency will be higher but you can validate inference results and prompts. it's common to start hosted then flip to Dedicated for perf.
[05:06] Carlos: another perf question: how do you handle batching vs latency for our real-time payouts flow
  we need sub-300ms 95th for short prompts (~150 tokens).
[05:16] Priya: for short prompts, continuous batching can be tuned aggressively with max latency SLO at 30-40ms to collect a few requests; but that increases latency for some. alternative is lower batch window and more Dedicated capacity to keep per-request latency low. we can do experiments: 1) tune batching small, 2) increase capacity, 3) use quantized model. we have bench configs for all three.
[05:36] Jordan: do you support per-route SLOs or per-API keys for routing to Dedicated vs hosted?
[05:43] Alex: yes, route by API key/route and we can set fallback policies
  if Dedicated unit is saturated we can fall back to hosted or a cheaper model variant. that's in the routing policy doc.
[05:51] Maya: any security caveats for fallback to hosted?
[05:54] Alex: yes you need to opt in for data egress to hosted if you want fallback; for regulated data you might prefer no fallback. we'll document that.
[05:59] Priya: quick note
  we saw a slight transcription artifact in last week's recording where "KV cash" was in the notes; just flagging that for the record.
[06:08] (laughter)
[06:10] Alex: ok final section
  blockers & risks. i see peering + KMS as primary. second is SOC2 sign-off if you want logs excluded. third small risk is model/regression risk
  we should run Eval set for your top 50 prompts.
[06:25] Carlos: we can share a sample eval set, maya will compile.
[06:29] Maya: yes i'll export top-50 user flows and share by Fri.
[06:33] Alex: perfect. any other questions?
[06:36] Carlos: pricing question
  can you confirm what committed reserved would look like? we need a rough ARR estimate for finance.
[06:43] Alex: we'll send a committed reserved slide with price breaks; rough numbers in doc I'll send today, committed per-month amortized for a 12 month term.
[06:52] Priya: also adding note
  quantization gave biggest cost wins in our runs, but you might see small generation quality diffs on some prompts; we'll include a few examples in the bench sheet.
[07:04] Maya: will you include the model variant names? we want to map to the ones in our eval harness.
[07:08] Priya: yes model tags and versions included.
[07:10] Alex: recap of next steps and who owns what
  Alex will send pricing + security pack and re-share bench sheet with perms; Priya will run the extra quantized run and post results; Jordan/Carlos will finish peering + KMS access; Maya will share eval set. we'll schedule the infra handoff next week.
[07:28] Carlos: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:31] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and update the ticket.
[07:34] Jordan: thanks.
[07:36] End of call.
